page: Microsoft Azure E16-8ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is 128.0 GB, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 614 GB SSD, and it is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Performance benchmarks place this server consistently in the average tier for most operations. The Intel processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1900.18 and a multi-core score of 7763.87, while Geekbench yields a single-core score of 1633.0 and a multi-core score of 6133.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 419.39 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 58.16 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 38.6 GB/sec for large-block writes. Database operations perform at an average level, with Passmark database operations scoring 4064.08 and Redis SET operations reaching 7.87 million operations per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and medium-sized (7B) LLM inference tasks represent performance bottlenecks, falling into the weak tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E16-8ds_v5 offers high memory density relative to its compute allocation, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU processing. The inclusion of a 614 GB local SSD provides fast temporary storage without requiring external disk attachments. This hardware profile is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data buffering, and general-purpose business applications requiring high memory-to-vCPU ratios.
